head: 82697cc
target: Aigent gains a headless evaluation layer for multeval: scenario files drive multi-step runs, every run lands as a result directory, and one check() judges any result directory from its files alone — the graded-files contract the multeval grader will read.
incidental: package.json and package-lock.json: the aigent bin entry and the npm script that loads .env (packaging)
test/boundary.test.ts: the import guard now also covers src/eval/ and fails if run.ts moves (guard upkeep)
the test fixtures, the weather.json example scenario and the new test files (scaffolding; the typed case-table guardrail is quizzed in q7)

questions.prompt: The old live test was a hard-coded weather script in TypeScript. Why is a scenario now a JSON file whose `expect` entries are named checks?

options.label: The model has to read the scenario to know which plugins it may enable
A multeval case hands aigent only a directory of files, and the named checks give the scenario, the report ids and the grader one shared vocabulary
Assertions in code cannot tell an engine bug from a model mistake, so they had to become data

key_points: multeval hands aigent files, not code: a case carries only the scenario's own directory, so the script must be data
the check names are one vocabulary shared by the scenario, the report ids (check@step) and the grader
each behavior sits beside the prompt step that must show it, so the file reads as the design's bets on the model

questions.prompt: `aigent run` finishes a run, writes the result directory, then grades readRun(out) — the files it just wrote, not the run it still holds in memory. What does that ordering protect?

options.label: Speed: grading the files skips re-parsing a transcript the runner already has
Safety: the in-memory run holds raw secrets the files do not
It proves the written files alone are enough to grade a run, so `aigent check`, the live test and the multeval grader all read the same files and get the same verdict

key_points: every run proves the directory alone is enough to grade it: a gap between what is written and what is graded cannot pass silently
every caller — the live test, `aigent check`, the future multeval grader — reads the same files and gets the same verdict
the result directory, not the in-memory run, is the contract multeval consumes

questions.prompt: check(run) judges three kinds of thing: invariants, behaviors and cost. Which of these are reasons for that split?

options.label: One failing invariant is an engine bug and fails the run, while a behavior is a bet on the model that lands in a rate
Behaviors are held out of the report until enough trials give them a trustworthy rate
The old live test asserted three ad hoc properties and logged the rest, so an engine bug and a model mistake looked alike
Cost is reported and never judged, so a contrast can still measure cached-token ratios without tuning them away

key_points: invariants are engine properties every trial must keep: one failure is an engine bug and gates the run
behaviors are the design's bets on the model, measured as rates; they never gate a run
cost is reported and never judged
before the split, an engine bug and a model mistake looked alike

questions.prompt: A run stops early — a step throws, say a resume whose plugin set rejects the saved records. What do the checks do with the behaviors on prompts that never ran, and what does that mean for the model's rates?

options.label: They fail, so a host-side crash cannot quietly flatter a model's rate
They skip, and a skip drags the rate down like a failure does
They skip, and a skipped trial is left out of its rate, so a rate counts only the trials that had the chance
Nothing is judged on an incomplete run: no report, no verdicts

key_points: a behavior whose step never ran skips; it does not fail
skipped trials are left out of the rate: a rate counts only trials that had the chance
the steps that ran are still written and checked, the report says the run is incomplete, and the invariants still run and never skip

questions.prompt: Before the first session opens, the runner refuses a run its environment or plugin sets cannot satisfy, and `aigent run` refuses an existing result directory before it even reads the scenario. Which of these hold about that up-front refusal?

options.label: A typo costs no model call: unset secrets, plugin sets that fail to load, and names the sets lack are all found before any session opens
The engine makes the same checks when the session is created, so the runner's pass is only a cache
Names are checked against the plugin set in effect at the step that relies on them, because a resume step can swap the set
Refusing the directory before reading the scenario means a repeated command never spends a model call

key_points: a misspelled name or unset secret must cost nothing: refusal happens before the first session opens
names are validated against the plugin set in effect at the step that uses them, since a resume can swap sets
the CLI refuses an existing out-dir before reading the scenario, so a repeat spends nothing
scenario problems are all reported at their JSON paths in one pass, so an author fixes a file in one round

questions.prompt: The engine already redacts what enters the conversation. Now an engine bug lets a raw secret value reach an event that listeners see. What happens between that event and anyone grading the run?

options.label: The engine's export redaction catches it on the way out, because events are redacted like the transcript

The runner scrubs every raw value out of the log into [LEAKED:NAME] marks before anything is written, the secret-free invariant fails as an engine bug, and a grader can see the leak without holding the key
The secret-free invariant skips: the leak is the engine's fault, not the model's, so the run had no chance to show it
The run passes and the cost section notes the leak

key_points: the runner scrubs every string of the run log before anything is written, so no raw value reaches the files
the [LEAKED:NAME] mark names the secret, so a grader can find a leak without the key
secret-free is an invariant: a leak is an engine bug that fails the run (exit 1), never a behavior or a note

questions.prompt: A new behavior arrives: after the model loads a skill, it should apply the skill's wording in its answer — check 'apply-skill', judged on the prompt step that asks for it. Where does it go, and what must land with it so the design holds?
key_points: the scenario layer gains the expectation variant with its fields, and the names it relies on join the pre-flight check, so a misspelled skill still costs no model call
checks.ts gains one judge for it; an expectation without a judge fails the build, so the check cannot land half
the behavior owns its skip rule: what its precondition is, and what happens when the precondition never occurred
both case tables are keyed by check name, so a passing and a failing case must be added or the tests do not compile
a scenario file writes the same check name, and its report id is apply-skill@<step>

questions.prompt: A run stops early, and the result directory it wrote also fails an invariant. What does `aigent run` print, and what does it exit with?

options.label: Exit 3: the run stopped early, and the invariant failure is only a detail inside the report
Exit 1 with nothing on stdout: an engine bug suppresses the report
The full report as JSON on stdout, exit 1: an invariant failure is an engine bug and wins over the incomplete run
Exit 2: a run that stops early is bad input, and nothing was written

key_points: the report is always printed as JSON on stdout
exit 1, an engine bug, wins over exit 3, an incomplete run
behaviors never move the exit code
2 means bad input found before anything ran, nothing written; 3 means the steps that ran were written and checked; 4 means the runner failed

questions.prompt: The run log keeps two views of one run: the transcript, and the events each step emitted. Which of these hold about why the checks read both?

options.label: No listener can see a session's creation-time records, so what a session had enabled at its start is read from the transcript
A core__call_tool rejected before it runs leaves no tool event, only an error result in the transcript, so dispatch-recover reads the transcript
The transcript is only a cache of the events, so a directory that loses transcript.json can be rebuilt from events.jsonl
The events group what a step did and carry each call's outcome, ran or denied, which the transcript alone does not show

key_points: creation-time records reach no listener, so per-session enabled-at-start comes from the transcript
a schema-rejected core__call_tool leaves an error result in the transcript and no tool event
events carry each step's emission order and each call's outcome; the result directory keeps both views

questions.prompt: Next in the design doc, the multeval adapter runs `aigent run` once per trial in a container and grades what comes back. Which parts of this change does it get for free, and where is its own work?
key_points: the result directory is the whole grading input: the adapter re-reads it and gets the same verdict `aigent run` printed, with no model and no secrets
exit codes sort trials for it: 1 an engine bug (fix aigent, not the model), 2 bad input, 3 incomplete but written, 4 runner failure; behavior rates come from the report, never the exit code
per-run verdicts are its to aggregate: rates over trials must leave skipped behaviors out, as check already does within a run
the directory is all-or-nothing and refuses to overwrite, so each trial needs a fresh out-dir and a crash leaves nothing to mistake for a run
a leak shows as a mark that names the secret, so the adapter needs no key to catch one
